name: end-to-end
title: One Script, End to End
kicker: Five services · one media type · every step offered by the last answer
html:
One Script, End to End

ServiceRelationWhat happens
1Release deskdesk:releaseA person asks; the desk starts ARTIE on the kept script
2Gatewayscm:pulls-getOpen the pull request
3Offer watchwatcher:watchTell me when it offers scm:merge; wait for the reply
4Gatewayscm:mergeMerge by squashing; check it’s merged
5CI · Jenkinsci:buildBuild the merge commit; wait for the reply
6CI · Jenkinsci:smoke-testRun the build’s own smoke scenarios against its deployment
7Dev, or the gatewayenv:promote or scm:commentAll passed: promote. One failed: say why on the pull request

Five services, one script written as data, one generic client.
say: Here's the whole release on one slide. A person asks the release desk to release a pull request: desk:release. The desk starts ARTIE on the kept script. ARTIE opens the pull request through the gateway, scm:pulls-get. It asks the watcher to say when merge is offered, and waits. Answered: it merges, scm:merge, by squashing, and checks the pull request really is merged. It asks CI to build the merge commit, ci:build, and waits. Answered: it follows the link to the build, and runs the smoke scenarios the build links, against the deployment the build links. If they all pass, it opens Dev and promotes the commit, env:promote, citing how many passed. If one fails, it doesn't promote; it says why on the pull request, scm:comment. Five services. One script, written as data. One generic client. And every step is a control the last answer offered.

deck:ref.name: right-behavior
deck:ref.label: RIGHT-BEHAVIOR
deck:ref.title: Right behavior: only what the state allows, and a reason when not
deck:ref.summary: The agent is offered only the acts the current state allows, sends each one with the validator from the state it read, and gets a reason when an act is absent. At the small scale it is a Gherkin scenario that says what right means before any code is written.

deck:ref.name: repeatability
deck:ref.label: REPEATABILITY
deck:ref.title: Repeatability: the same goal, the same result, every time
deck:ref.summary: Given the same inputs, the same outputs, call after call. Found once with a model, then replayed with none: the same steps, the same checks, the same result, until the controls really change. At the small scale it is one scenario that runs the same way every time.

deck:ref.name: resilience
deck:ref.label: RESILIENCE
deck:ref.title: Resilience: the server changes, the client doesn't break
deck:ref.summary: When the server changes, or misbehaves on purpose, the client takes the failure path the spec names, re-syncs, and goes on; a model comes back only when the controls really changed, to repair. At the small scale it is the regression suite and the gates that hold, even against the model.

deck:ref.name: rise
deck:ref.label: RISE
deck:ref.title: RISE: tell me when it's done
deck:ref.summary: Reciprocal Interface for State Exchange. Replies for asynchronous work: ask now, be told later. A watcher or a build answers back when it is ready, as Jenkins does in the release.
